Total area:

parts.latex:
Find the area of triangle PQR, correct to the nearest square metre.

\exfigure{3296_q7d_1}

solutions.latex:
Use the cosine rule to find angle $R$:
$$166^2 = 100^2+80^2-2\times100\times80\cos R$$
$$\cos R = -0.69725,\qquad R = 134.206\ldots^\circ$$
Then the area formula:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area} &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times100\times80\times\sin 134.206\ldots^\circ \\ &= 2867.312\ldots \\ &\approx 2867 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes the cosine rule equation, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle ABC with sides 16, 18 and angles 47 and 32 degrees

parts.latex:
\exfigure{706_q10_1}

What is the area of the triangle $ABC$? (Answer correct to 2 significant figures).

solutions.latex:
Two angles are given, so first find $\angle B$ using the angle sum of a triangle.
$$\angle B = 180^\circ - 47^\circ - 32^\circ = 101^\circ$$
The sides $AB = 16$ and $BC = 18$ enclose $\angle B$, so use the area formula $A = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 16\times 18\times\sin 101^\circ\\ &\approx 141.4 \text{ cm}^2\\ &\approx 140 \text{ cm}^2 \text{ (2 significant figures)} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{area} \approx 140 \text{ cm}^2$$

figures.cap: triangle with sides 30, x, 28 and angle 44 degrees

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$:
$$\begin{aligned} 250 &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 30 \times x \times \sin 44^\circ \\ 250 &= 15 \times x \times \sin 44^\circ \\ x &= \dfrac{250}{15 \times \sin 44^\circ} \\ &= 23.99260899\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x = 24 \text{ cm}$$
criteria: Correct area equation, or equivalent merit

\exfigure{706_q31_1}

The flag shown above has three sections. $\triangle ABC$ is right-angled with $AC = 120$ cm and $BC = 45$ cm. The distances $BD$, $DE$ and $EC$ are equal and $\angle DEA = 105^\circ$.

figures.cap: flag with triangle ABC and points D, E on BC

parts.latex: Calculate the distance $AE$. Answer correct to nearest centimetre.
Find the area of the $\triangle DEA$. Answer correct to the nearest square centimetre.
What percentage of the area of the banner is the $\triangle DEA$? Answer correct to one decimal place.

solutions.latex:
$$BD = DE = EC = \dfrac{45}{3} = 15 \text{ cm}$$
$\triangle ACE$ is right-angled at $C$, so by Pythagoras' theorem:
$$\begin{aligned} AE^2 &= 15^2 + 120^2 \\ AE &= \sqrt{15^2 + 120^2} \\ &= 120.9338662\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ AE = 121 \text{ cm}$$
Alternatively, $\sin 75^\circ = \dfrac{120}{AE}$.

Using the area formula $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ with $DE = 15$ and $AE = 120.9338662\ldots$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area of } \triangle DEA &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 15 \times 120.9338662\ldots \times \sin 105^\circ \\ &= 876.0985849\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Area of } \triangle DEA = 876 \text{ cm}^2$$
criteria: Correct area equation, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The banner is $\triangle ABC$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area of } \triangle ABC &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 120 \times 45 \\ &= 2700 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Percentage} &= \dfrac{876.0985849\ldots}{2700} \times 100 \\ &= 32.44809574\ldots\% \\ &\approx 32.4\% \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \triangle DEA \text{ is } 32.4\% \text{ of the banner}$$
criteria: Area of $\triangle ABC$, or equivalent merit
